intro: Covers forming and using the past perfect (had + past participle) in context.

items.q: By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film ___.
items.why: Past perfect shows the film finished before another past event.

items.q: She felt sick because she ___ too much at the party.
items.why: Past perfect shows the cause happened before the result.

items.q: ___ you ever visited that city before you moved there?
items.why: Past perfect question form uses had + subject + past participle.

items.q: He didn't recognise her because they ___ for twenty years.
items.why: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle for earlier unfulfilled action.

items.q: After the guests ___, we started cleaning the house.
items.why: Past perfect in after-clause shows the first completed action.

parts.title: Complete the sentences with the correct form.

items.pre: When I got to the station, the train
items.post: and I had to wait an hour.
items.why: Past perfect shows the train left before the speaker arrived.

items.pre: They couldn't get in because they
items.why: Past perfect explains the reason for a past situation.

items.post: sushi before I went to Japan.
items.why: Negative past perfect with never before a past experience.

items.pre: By the time she was thirty, she
items.why: Past perfect with by the time shows completion before a past point.
Past perfect shows an earlier unnoticed action affecting the present past moment.
Just with past perfect shows very recent completion before another past event.

parts.title: Find and correct the mistake in each sentence.

items.sentence: She already left when her friend called her.
items.corrected: She had already left when her friend called her.
items.why: Past perfect needed to show departure happened before the phone call.

items.sentence: By the time he arrived, we waited for two hours.
items.corrected: By the time he arrived, we had waited for two hours.
items.why: By the time signals the first action must use past perfect.

items.sentence: I didn't eat lunch because I have had a big breakfast.
items.corrected: I didn't eat lunch because I had had a big breakfast.
items.why: Past perfect, not present perfect, needed to link two past events.

parts.title: Write your own sentences.
parts.pointsLabel: 2 points: 1 for correct form, 1 for meaning and use

items.prompt: Write a sentence about something you had already done before you started learning English.
items.criteria: Correct use of past perfect (had + past participle); a clear time reference to a past moment.
items.example: I had already studied French for two years before I started learning English.

items.prompt: Write a sentence describing how you felt after something had happened to you in the past, explaining the reason with the past perfect.
items.criteria: Two past events in correct sequence; past perfect for the earlier event; a cause-and-effect link.
items.example: I felt exhausted because I had worked twelve hours without a break.
